title: Implement debounced escalation + impact-tagging to reduce noisy SLO alerts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During the capacity regression on 2026-02-25 we observed a high volume of short-lived SLO alerts that caused multiple escalations and duplication of engineering effort. Root cause analysis shows the noisy signals were primarily driven by transient latency spikes during autoscaler-driven VM/GPU resizing and by a lack of request-context in our SLO detector. This ticket implements two complementary mitigations: 1) a debounce/hysteresis layer on escalation paths to avoid repeated paging for the same short-lived condition, and 2) enrichment of alert signals with lightweight impact tags (percent-serving-loss, affected-route, request-concurrency-bucket) so downstream on-call can triage and prioritize without immediate escalation.
background: What happened: multiple SLO alerts fired within seconds as nodes came and went; our current escalation immediately pages SRE for each distinct alert signal. Noise vectors: (a) transient kernel warm-up and KV cache miss storms during scale-ups; (b) short-lived queueing at ingress as new worker pods drain; (c) lack of a correlate field that groups alerts by causal footprint. Why it matters: repeated pages during the same incident cost minutes of context-switching, delay remediation for real incidents, and increase operational costs for Dedicated customers who rely on SLAs.
action_items: 1) Implement Escalation Debounce: Add a configurable per-alert-key debounce window (default 3m) that suppresses re-paging for alerts with the same causal fingerprint. 2) Introduce Hysteresis Thresholds: Require a sustained exceedance (e.g., 60s) or a second confirming sample within the window before triggering page. 3) Signal Enrichment: Add impact tags to SLO alerts: "pct_serving_loss", "top_route", "median_latency_ms", "scale_event_id". 4) Alert Prioritization Rules: Route low-impact (>95% serving, latency spike <5s) to non-paged channel with auto-throttle. 5) Dashboard & Monitoring: Build an "Escalation Health" dashboard tracking alert volume, unique escalation keys, pages/hour, and median time between repeated pages. 6) Runbook updates: Document new thresholds, how to bypass debounce for critical customers, and how to interpret impact tags. 7) Post-deploy experiment: Run for 2 weeks in read-only mode (no suppression) to validate signal enrichment correctness, then enable suppression behind feature flag, start with 1 region canary.
acceptance_criteria:
- Reduction in repeated paged alerts by >=70% for matched fingerprints in a 7d rolling window.
- No increase in missed critical incidents: confirmed by comparing true-positive incident detections before/after for top-10 customers.
- Feature gated rollout with per-team opt-out.
- Dashboard shows correct tagging on historical alerts and ability to filter by tags.
- Runbook updated, on-call briefed, and SLO regression test executed in staging.
implementation_notes:
Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Debounced+Escalation+and+Impact+Tags (see section 'Fingerprinting and Key Selection').
Prototype PR for debounce algorithm: https://github.com/redwood-inference/alerting/pull/4251.
Fingerprint heuristic: prefer (project, route-pattern, scale_event_id, anomaly_window_start) and fall back to host-group when missing. Keep fingerprint TTL = 10m.
Feature flag: runtime.feature_flags.debounce_escalation with region-scoped config.
Telemetry: increment metrics 'escalation.suppressed', 'escalation.debounce_window_ms', and attach 'impact_tag.*' labels.
rollout_plan:
1) Merge PR and run unit/integration tests. 2) Canary in us-west-2 for non-critical customers for 48h. 3) If metrics stable, enable for all hosted API traffic in us-west-2 for 7d. 4) Enable in additional regions incrementally. 5) Monitor escalation health dashboard and customer SLO metrics; rollback flag if missed-critical-incidents >1 in 7d.
Rollback: flip runtime.feature_flags.debounce_escalation=false and remove suppression hooks; immediate alert if suppression metric spikes incorrectly.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for debounce logic, TTL, and fingerprint collisions.
- Integration test that simulates a scale-up event and verifies only one page within the debounce window.
- Load test with synthetic traffic to ensure metric cardinality remains bounded when adding impact tags.
- Chaos test: simulate quick flapping to validate hysteresis prevents repeated pages but still surfaces sustained outages.
monitoring_and_metrics: Primary: alert_count_total, unique_escalation_keys, escalation_pages_per_hour, escalation_suppressed_total. Secondary: true_positive_incident_rate, mean_time_to_ack, customer_error_rate_by_route. Dashboards: Escalation Health (by region), Impact Tag distribution, Debounce window effectiveness. Links: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/alerts/escalation-health
risk_and_mitigation: Risks: (1) Over-suppression may hide genuine incidents — mitigate with conservative default windows and an override for critical customers. (2) Increased metric cardinality from tags — mitigate by bucketing values and limiting tag set to 4 small-cardinality fields. (3) Fingerprint collisions causing unrelated alerts to be grouped — mitigate by including scale_event_id and route-pattern in primary fingerprint and keeping TTL short (10m).
communication: Announce to on-call channel and engineering-all with rollout timeline and opt-out instructions. Schedule 30m on-call briefing once canary begins. Add note to status-page incase customers ask about changes to paging behavior.
comments: 2026-02-28 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after postmortem for 2026-02-25 capacity regression. Initial proposal to combine debounce + tagging. Tagged with SRE for design review.

2026-03-02 - Sofia Jensen: Design review complete. Recommended 180s default debounce, 60s confirming sample hysteresis. Agreed to limit initial impact tags to pct_serving_loss, top_route, and scale_event_id to control cardinality.
2026-03-04 - Marco Li: Prototype implemented and pushed as PR #4251. Unit tests added. Requesting review from infra-alerting and SRE owners.

2026-03-06 - Rajiv Menon (SRE): Reviewed. Concern about critical-customer opt-out and how Dedicated customers will be handled — suggested per-customer override in routing table. Added dependency on ENG-45109 for routing config UI.
2026-03-08 - Marco Li: Addressed comments, added feature flag and telemetry for suppressed counts. Integration tests green on staging. Preparing canary in us-west-2 next week.
2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Confirmed schedule for canary start 2026-03-12. Noted runbook update assigned to support team (Sofia).

2026-03-12 - Marco Li: Canary started in us-west-2 for 48 hours. Early telemetry: escalation_suppressed_total=112 (first 6h), unique_escalation_keys down 62% relative to baseline. Monitoring for missed-critical-incidents ongoing.
due_notes: Plan to finish rollout and documentation by end of March. Will collect 14 days of post-rollout metrics before closing the ticket.
expected_outcome: Significant reduction in noisy escalations, improved on-call focus, and clearer triage data through impact tags. No measurable increase in missed critical events.
